text:
jamie: FYI support hit a bug: rotating REDWOOD_API_KEY in /etc/redwood/env doesn't update a running service -> 401s until restart. Anyone seen this?

alex: Yep. Processes only read env on startup. systemd env-file updates don't propagate. Containers too.

maria: Ouch. Repro?

jamie: echo 'REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_old' > /etc/redwood/env; start service; rotate file to sk_new; requests fail until restart.

suresh: We added credentials.refresh() in Node but Go/Python lack parity. Long-lived streams embed token in metadata and keep failing.

maria: Short-term: SIGHUP handler to reload the env file and call provider.refresh(). For k8s/docker, provide file-watch option.

alex: Implementation: provider should read from an atomic pointer so middleware/streams pick up new key without races. Prefer inotify, fall back to SIGHUP. Avoid busy polling.

jamie: Can we add a CLI opt `--cred-watch=/path` to opt into auto-reload? Low-friction for customers mounting secrets.

suresh: I'll draft a tiny RFC + PR: add refresh() in Go/Python, `--cred-watch` and `--env-sighup`, filewatch impl + SIGHUP fallback, tests for mid-stream rotation.

rotations-bot: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/684

maria: Add a sample-app README snippet showing systemd + SIGHUP and a docker kill -s HUP example.

jamie: Prioritize next sprint if possible; causing onboarding pain.
